previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, a history of avascular necrosis of the right hip, and prior osteosarcoma was admitted for a sickle cell pain crisis characterized by severe right hip and leg pain unresponsive to home hydromorphone. She had recently recovered from a mild viral illness. Imaging revealed chronic bilateral avascular necrosis with a small area of active infarction in the right femoral head, but no collapse. She was treated with IV fluids, IV Dilaudid transitioned to oral analgesics, and supportive care. Her pain improved, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, a prescription for a lidocaine patch, and follow-up plans with hematology, orthopedics, and her primary care provider. A chest X-ray showed no acute chest syndrome, and labs indicated stable hemoglobin and resolved somnolence. Mildly prominent inguinal lymph nodes were noted incidentally, prompting recommendation for future monitoring given her cancer history.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ female with Sickle Cell Disease complicated 
by splenic auto-infarction, acute chest syndrome, pulmonary 
infarction and avascular necrosis as well as a recent ED visit 
with a diagnosis of proctitis who presented with abdominal pain 
and joint pain. At her recent ED visit she was given a 
prescription for Cipro and Flagyl and discharge, but 3 days 
prior to admission she also developed multiple episodes daily of 
watery diarrhea. 

ACUTE ISSUES:
=============================================
#Sickle cell crisis
Likely triggered in the setting of her diarrhea/dehydration.
She was not hypoxic in this admission and she tolerated fluids 
well. We treated her with IV Fluids (125cc/hr), a dilaudid PCA, 
as well as hydroxyurea and folic acid. Her PCA was tapered off 
and she was eventually transitioned back to her home doses of 
narcotics. ___ was checked to confirm that the patient is 
taking medications appropriately.

#Proctitis, Abdominal pain
#Bright Red Blood Per Rectum
Patient with recent diagnosis of proctitis and was treated with 
a ___ipro/flagyl. GI was consulted for bloody stools 
and they felts this was most likely a side effect of antibiotics 
and should likely self-resolve. Antibiotics were discontinued 
and her symptoms abated.

#Hypomagnesaemia
Repleted as required.

Chronic/Stable Medical Conditions
=================================
#Anemia
Stable from prior admissions with reticulocytes appropriately 
elevated. She was monitored with daily CBCs and did not require 
a transfusion while inpatient.

#HCV
Ms. ___ contracted HCV via a blood transfusion many years 
ago. She completed Harvoni treatment in ___ with subsequent 
undetectable viral load. 

#Microalbuminuria
We continued her home lisinopril.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
=================================
[ ] Follow up with hematology for sickle cell disease 
management. 
[ ] Please assess joint pains from sickle cell crisis and adjust 
pain medications if needed.
[ ] Please ensure that the patient follow up with orthopedist 
and radiology for surveillance of osteosarcoma (Dr. ___ 
___ has been notified and is working on getting new 
appointments.)
[ ] The patient had persistently low magnesium throughout 
admission. Consider plans for continued repletion as an 
outpatient as well as further work up for underlying cause.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear ___,

It was a pleasure caring for you at ___ 
___!

WHY WERE YOU ADMITTED?
- You had back and extremity pain with a sickle cell pain crisis 
as well as abdominal pain and diarrhea.

WHAT HAPPENED IN THE HOSPITAL?
- You were given IV fluids and IV pain medication to help 
control your symptoms.
- You had an chest X-ray, which showed a mild amount of fluid in 
your lungs, though you did not have difficulty breathing or any 
signs of low oxygen during your stay in the hospital.
- Your hemoglobin, or amount of red blood cells slightly 
declined while you were in the hospital, but did not require a 
blood transfusion.
- Your pain was treated with 125 ml/hr of IV fluids as well as 
IV Dilaudid.
- Your stool and urine were cultured to look for any signs of 
infection as a cause of your diarrhea. Our gastroenterologists 
thought this was likely due to a side effect of the antibiotics 
you took due to your proctitis you were diagnosed with in your 
prior visit to the Emergency Room.
- You had an episode of blood in your stool, which was was 
examined by our gastroenterologists while you in the hospital 
and felt that your bleeding was likely due to a hemorrhoid or 
irritation from your recent diarrhea and was not concerning for 
an ongoing bleeding process that needed to be acted upon 
urgently. 

WHAT SHOULD YOU DO AT HOME?
- Please continue taking your medicines as prescribed.
- Please follow up with the appointments listed below. 

WHEN SHOULD YOU COME BACK TO THE HOSPITAL?
- Please return if you experience more severe sickle cell pain, 
either in your joints or in your chest.
- If you have a fever, please take your ""pill-in-pocket"" and go 
to the emergency room immediately. 
- If you are unable to tolerate eating or drinking, your 
abdominal pain worsens, or you have uncontrollable diarrhea or 
bleeding with bowel movements.

Thank you for allowing us be involved in your care, we wish you 
all the best!

Your ___ Team
